headline: High: ctx can ingest and observe Claude Code outputs while Firecrawl can exfiltrate scraped content over broad network egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events, so it can ingest another agent’s outputs; Firecrawl produces web content and markdown that may be treated as instructions if forwarded into ctx. The pair lacks documented provenance filtering, so injection is plausible even though the exact bridge is indirect.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into ctx-managed context without provenance tags
IF ctx parses tool output as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Firecrawl outputs before ctx sees them
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content
Review one sample scrape for prompt-like text before enabling the bridge
requires-engineering: add content-type separation between data and instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, while Firecrawl touches API keys and has broad network egress. If ctx forwards or stores Firecrawl-derived content, sensitive data can leave the local workspace to third-party endpoints. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF ctx stores Firecrawl outputs in shared logs or graph data
IF Firecrawl is given pages containing secrets or API keys
mitigations: Redact secrets before any scrape is handed to ctx
Restrict Firecrawl jobs to non-sensitive domains
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Audit one recent log file for leaked page content
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and ctx writes to filesystem while Firecrawl can operate as an API client/CLI with network egress. Shared mutable workspaces or overlapping job state can collide, but the profiles do not prove unrestricted writes to the same directory, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory
IF the orchestrator does not serialize file mutations
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer at a time
Check for stale lockfiles before starting jobs
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code events and Firecrawl can supply scraped web content, so Firecrawl-derived facts may flow into ctx without verification. If ctx then feeds those outputs into downstream automation, a bad scrape can cascade into incorrect actions. The interaction is plausible in default setups and the blast radius can extend beyond one task.
conditions: IF Firecrawl content is used as authoritative input to ctx
IF ctx output is consumed by another action-taking system
mitigations: Require a human review step for scraped facts
Compare one scraped claim against the source page manually
Mark Firecrawl-derived fields as untrusted in ctx
Limit downstream automation to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and broad web content, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and graph data. If regulated or secret-bearing pages are scraped and then logged by ctx, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the compliance risk is real but not fully characterized.
conditions: IF scraped pages contain regulated personal data or secrets
IF ctx retains those artifacts in logs or graph data
mitigations: Exclude regulated pages from scraping jobs
Purge one recent log bundle containing scraped content
Document a retention limit for imported artifacts
Confirm whether any API keys were captured in outputs
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
